name: Academic researcher
goals: Measure what the protocols actually carry: real agent counts, real payment volume, Sybil rates, failure rates.
Formally analyze authorization and payment protocols for replay, binding and atomicity properties.
Model the economics: fee floors, two-sided platform power, and who captures surplus in agent commerce.
Build reproducible datasets and benchmarks that others can rerun as the specs change.
Connect current designs to prior work on micropayments, reputation systems and bot authentication.
pains: Headline metrics (agents registered, payments processed) are inflated by placeholders and farming, and the sources dispute each other.
Specs change faster than peer review. A result on one dated version is stale by publication.
Proprietary specs and read-only repositories limit what can be studied and reproduced.
On-chain data is public but off-chain checkout traffic (ACP, UCP) is private, so measurements skew toward crypto rails.
Protocols reuse names for different things (ACP, MPP, agentic token), which makes literature search and comparison error-prone.
decisions: Which protocol version and chain set to study, and how to date the snapshot.
Which measurement methodology to adopt for liveness, Sybil detection and volume adjustment.
Which formal model and tool to use for protocol analysis.
How to publish data and code so the result survives spec changes.
